research_question: In children with otitis media with effusion (OME), does autoinflation (Valsalva-type middle ear inflation through the nose using a balloon, carnival blower or commercial device), compared with watchful waiting or no treatment, reduce the proportion with persistent middle ear effusion at the first follow-up at or before 6 weeks?
treatment_label: Autoinflation (nasal balloon, carnival blower or commercial autoinflation device)
control_label: Watchful waiting / no treatment / standard care only
outcome_description: Number of children (or ears, as reported) with persistent middle ear effusion at the first follow-up at or before 6 weeks, out of the number randomised in each arm. Persistence is defined as a flat (type B) tympanogram, type B or C2 tympanogram, or effusion still visible on pneumatic otoscopy; resolution/improvement is its complement (if a paper reports numbers resolved or improved, convert to persistence as total minus resolved). Use the follow-up closest to 4 weeks within the 2-6 week window; if several times are reported in that window, use the latest one. Prefer per-child data; if only per-ear data are reported for children with bilateral disease, divide both events and totals by the design effect 1 + (average ears per child - 1) x 0.5 and note that the adjustment was applied.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g (equivalently RR < 1) means autoinflation produced less persistent middle ear effusion than watchful waiting/no treatment at up to 6 weeks, i.e. the result favours autoinflation.
search_queries: autoinflation otitis media with effusion randomised trial children
nasal balloon Politzer middle ear inflation glue ear controlled trial
autoinflation tympanogram resolution effusion children outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in children (under 18 years) with otitis media with effusion / glue ear

Compares an autoinflation intervention (nasal balloon, carnival blower, or commercial autoinflation device) with watchful waiting, no treatment or standard care only (multi-arm trials: autoinflation and no-treatment arms only)
Reports any quantitative data allowing calculation of the proportion with persistent or resolved middle ear effusion (tympanometry or pneumatic otoscopy) at a follow-up at or before 6 weeks
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, narrative review, theoretical or methodological paper); duplicate reports of the same trial are counted once, although a separate pilot trial reported in the same document counts as its own study

No comparison between autoinflation and an untreated control condition (e.g. control is sham autoinflation, placebo, or another active treatment; or autoinflation given as an add-on to other treatment in only one arm)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no events/totals, proportions, means+SDs, t/F values or odds ratios for effusion persistence at or before 6 weeks)

Unrelated to the research topic: adults, surgical treatments (grommets/ventilation tubes, adenoidectomy), or outcomes limited to hearing, symptoms, quality of life, adverse events, or persistence only at 6 weeks to 3 months or later
moderators_to_extract: Autoinflation device type (nasal balloon vs carnival blower vs commercial device)
Unit of analysis (per child vs per ear with design-effect adjustment)
Diagnostic criterion for persistence (type B tympanogram, B or C2, pneumatic otoscopy)
Exact follow-up timing within the 2-6 week window
Sample size category and risk of bias / allocation concealment
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio with a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML), events = children (or design-effect-adjusted ears) with persistent effusion, totals = number per arm. RR < 1 favours autoinflation. Per-ear data adjusted by the design effect 1 + (mean ears per child - 1) x 0.5; per-child data preferred where both are available.
single_outcome_target: persistent otitis media with effusion at up to 6 weeks
